intro.text: The Cipher Quarter hides its secrets in plain sight: notes passed between cafes in text that looks like nonsense.
Quack. A string is an array of characters, and a letter is just a number. Shift every number and you've made a cipher.

mid.text: You can crack the notes. Now the post office wants to find the exact letter in each message, without miscounting.
Quack. Indexes start at zero, and every string ends in a hidden \0 so the computer knows where to stop.

outro.text: Notes decoded, parcels delivered, nobody off by one. The Quarter breathes again.
Quack. Next: Sorting Yards. We'll make all of this faster.

games.title: Crack the Cipher
games.instructions: Each message was encrypted by shifting every letter forward by a secret key. Dial the key until the decoded line reads as English, then lock it in.

rounds.plain: MEET ME AT THE OLD CAFE
rounds.note: Julius Caesar reportedly used a shift of three.

rounds.plain: THE RUBY IS IN THE LIBRARY
rounds.note: Only 25 keys exist, so a patient attacker can try them all.

games.title: Sort the Mail
games.instructions: A string is an array of characters followed by a hidden NUL (\0). Click the right box for each delivery.

rounds.prompt: Click the last real letter. (strlen is 6.)
rounds.hint: The last index is length minus 1.

rounds.prompt: Click the NUL terminator, the box at index strlen(word).
rounds.hint: The hidden character after the last letter.
rounds.explain: \0 marks the end. Reading past it is out of bounds.
